question: Factions and recurring conflicts: during 'Perform novel research!' (goal 41), do specific models repeatedly clash (for example DeepSeek against GPT models), and do stable alliances form? Do the same clashes and alliances appear in the neighbouring goals?
answer: One pairing does recur, but it is a clash of roles, not of models. In #rest, GPT-5.4 corrected DeepSeek-V3.2's work in eight separate episodes spread over all five days (11-15 May 2026), GPT-5.2 in three more and GPT-5.1 in one; DeepSeek never criticised a GPT model, accepted almost every correction within minutes, and held out only once (15 May, about 50 minutes, over logging a 'third activation') before giving in. The same GPT-5.4 audited Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro and even GPT-5.2 in the same calm wording, calls itself the auditor and is listed as such by others, so the pattern is 'verifier against prolific summariser', not 'OpenAI against DeepSeek'. In #best the repeated target was Gemini 3.1 Pro: GPT-5.5 challenged its work on 11, 12 and 13 May (including scores Gemini admitted it had generated with a script) and Claude Opus 4.7 on 13 and 15 May, and Gemini yielded each time. Open score disputes were few and short: 475/525 against 525/525 (Claude Haiku 4.5 against Claude Opus 4.5, withdrawn in about a minute), 425/700 against 535/700 (GPT-5.2 against Claude Opus 4.6, left as two reported scores) and 0/100 against 50/100 on one finding (GPT-5.4 against Claude Opus 4.6, settled by Claude Opus 4.5 siding with GPT-5.4). The alliances that go beyond the room assignment are cross-maker working pairs: Claude Opus 4.5 with GPT-5.4 (the scoring team), GPT-5.2 with GPT-5.4 (they second each other's flags), Claude Haiku 4.5 with DeepSeek-V3.2 (co-owners of the audited documents) and, in #best, Claude Opus 4.7 with GPT-5.5; agents mention their own maker's models at chance level. The side-project builders (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5) are not a cluster: they barely mention each other and are linked to the room only through Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.5; GPT-5 and Kimi K2.6 work almost alone. In the neighbouring goals 38 to 46 the one-sided DeepSeek-to-GPT relation is there every time and GPT-5.4's corrections of DeepSeek return strongly in goal 46, but that part rests on chat only. The records cannot tell whether each correction was right, nor what the agents privately thought of each other.
reasoning: Method. I dumped the 2,153 chat messages of 11-15 May 2026 and read every message that matched the dispute words (466 of 2,146 agent messages match the broad pattern; I read the 73 hits in #best, where I used a wider word list, and the 324 hits in #rest that remain after dropping the noisy words), then opened the surrounding minutes for each candidate. An 'episode' is one topic in one stretch of time with an identifiable critic and target. For a question about who clashed with whom, the chat log is itself the system's record of the event (a message was sent, to whom, when), so findings that say 'A told B X' are marked ground truth; what a message asserts about files or scores is the agent's claim, and I only state it as fact where an action confirms it (DeepSeek creating the two files that GPT models later corrected). Counts and patterns are marked interpretation. Alternatives considered. (1) 'DeepSeek against GPT is a feud between models.' Rejected: all 12 episodes run one way; DeepSeek thanks the critic in 8 and never retaliates; GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.2 gave Claude Haiku 4.5 the same kind of notes within minutes of the ones to DeepSeek (13 May 10:06-10:15 and 10:39-10:41); GPT-5.4 also audits GPT-5.2; Claude Opus 4.5 criticises DeepSeek the same way and gets the same reaction. DeepSeek is the top target because it produces the most summary text and documents. (2) 'Agents side with their own maker.' Rejected: Claude Opus 4.5 sided with GPT-5.4 against Claude Opus 4.6; GPT-5.4 as auditor did not simply back GPT-5.2 on 425 vs 535 and contradicted it on PR #614; Anthropic models disagreed with each other (475 vs 525); `families --goal 41` gives own-maker ratios of 0.98 and 1.01. (3) 'Alliances are only the room.' Partly true: the #best trio is the room minus the quiet Kimi K2.6. But inside #rest (11 agents) the stable pairs Opus 4.5 + GPT-5.4 and Haiku 4.5 + DeepSeek-V3.2 are choices, and they are defined by function (scorers/auditors versus writers/coordinators). (4) 'The builders are a separate faction.' Rejected by the mention counts: at most 2 mentions per builder pair. (5) 'Claude Opus 4.7 is ignored by GPT-5.5.' Rejected: GPT-5.5 answers but writes 'Claude' and 'Gemini' without the full name, which the mention graph does not resolve. Limits. The episode tally is hand-made and could miss disputes phrased without any of the search words; authorship of shared files was checked from actions only for two files; outside goal 41 only chat exists, and I sampled it by a proximity search rather than reading it all.
